periods.summary: Naseem answers Or-Gaule's invitation in exchange for the right to take Vermillion and Quedland after their collapse. He saves Or-Gaule by ambushing Wallenshtein from inside the old swordsman's body and dehydrating him into a mummy. At Caldia he appears on the west avenue, defeats Dandallion and many soldiers, and fights Stella with only his left hand at first. His punches are impossibly heavy because his true nature is not simple sand manipulation but dehydration: he removes water and turns matter, bodies, and even ground into dead sand. Stella identifies part of the trick but is unable to stop his right-handed escalation. Nene Saikyo's meteor/gravity intervention prevents his strike from devastating the area; he reveals the scale of his Haboob-like ability, then prepares to fight Nene before Or-Gaule interrupts.

key_events.summary: Kills Wallenshtein by ambush to save Or-Gaule and joins the new faction.

His fight with Nene is suspended by Or-Gaule's announcement.

periods.summary: Naseem reacts furiously when Or-Gaule and Lunaeyes halt the Caldia battle, grabbing Or-Gaule and threatening to kill him for spoiling his fight with Nene. Or-Gaule pacifies him by proposing that League members already in Vermillion may join the representative war, giving Naseem a legal battlefield against Night Princess without League interference. He then disperses as sand and returns to Quedland. His presence as a Quedland representative and as one of the Desperado-class threats is central to Stella and Nene's urgent training.

periods.summary: On the night before the representative war, Naseem appears alone before the League army massed on the Quedland border and issues a withdrawal ultimatum as Quedland's envoy. Commander Dargus uses the talks to prepare a tank barrage and blows apart what seems to be Naseem's body, but the remains turn into black sand and reform. Naseem mocks ordinary common sense, makes a gun from earth with Alchimia Hierro, and slaughters advance troops while bullets pass through his particle body. When Mage-Knights surround him, he invokes Mictlan Tormenta, a sandstorm that is truly the release of desiccating power, drying nearby fighters into dust and routing the army. Carlo Bertoni arrives with the water domain Eighth Sea and initially traps him, using supercavitation attacks, ice spears and a heart-piercing thrust. Naseem nevertheless drinks the sea dry, treats lethal wounds as entertainment, crushes Carlo's head, and collapses the ground into quicksand to bury much of the assault force. Afterward he tells Or-Gaule that League and Union idealists are boring, but Nene Saikyo's eyes interest him. At the war opening he rushes first, scatters the Vermillion team with Mictlan Tormenta, and immediately clashes with Nene in a Desperado-level melee that turns the gate area into an apocalyptic zone.

periods.summary: Naseem faces Nene in the wasteland created by his opening Mictlan Tormenta. His left jab wall, Dead End Blow and Hyper War Sense counter her gravity swordplay, and even after Nene cuts him apart he survives by reconstituting his body from sand. Excited that Nene can approach his death, he tears off his own face and enters Overdrive, becoming a demon-like monster with golden flame-like magic, wings, horns and a tail. In this state he destroys Nene's full Hadou Tensei meteor barrage with Mictlan Tormenta, shatters her spiritual device, and forces her own oni-like Overdrive. At first he enjoys the monster duel, but Nene's latent magic and gravity overwhelm him: his limbs and tail are crushed, his regeneration is pinned by Jibakujin, and he experiences genuine fear of death. When Nene voluntarily returns to human form he thinks she has thrown away victory, only to be trapped by her new Hanten Fukuchi, a spatial-node technique that drags him into compactified higher-dimensional space. He panics, begs her at least to kill him, and disappears from the battlefield.

key_events.summary: Uses Overdrive to become a demon and forces Nene into her own oni-like awakening.
Falls for Nene's final trap and is exiled from normal space.
